units.title: Health
units.intro: This unit asks: **what is health?** You will read three short stories (case studies), think about **health and gender**, **rules of health**, and a **health promoting school**.

pins.text: Case I: Ato Habte, 40, rich; eats and drinks a lot, goes to bars; a fierce father
Case II: Halima, grade 7, very clever; has a twisted leg; boys tease her
Case III: W/ro Almaz, 35, a widow with six children; works hard; sometimes lonely and sad

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: You will learn the **broad meaning of health**.
You will practise **life skills** and **healthy behaviour**.

cards.title: Three case studies
body: Tap each person. Read each story.

cards.title: Case I: Ato Habte
body: Ato Habte is **40** and very **rich**. He skips breakfast at home.
At work he orders **two dishes of zigni** and **two bottles of beer**.
He drinks in bars every evening and has risky relationships, though he always uses a condom.
At home he is a **fierce father**. His children are afraid of him.

cards.title: Case II: Halima
body: Halima is in **grade 7**. She is very **clever** and reads all the time.
Boys say she won't dance because of her **twisted leg**.
Halima says **their minds are more twisted than her leg**. But she wishes she had a good leg.

cards.title: Case III: W/ro Almaz
body: W/ro Almaz is **35**, a **widow** with **six children**. Her husband died in the **liberation war**.
She works hard in a **textile factory** but is poor. All her children go to school.
The children grow **vegetables** and raise **chickens**. The family **loves each other** and prays every day.
Sometimes she feels **lonely and sad**.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: The book asks: **Who is more healthy? Why?**
How could each person **improve** his or her health?

cards.title: Three aspects of health
body: The book names three aspects of health.

cards.title: Memory trick: P-M-S
body: Health = **P**hysical + **M**ental + **S**ocial.

cards.title: Your health
body: Which aspect (**physical, mental or social**) is most difficult for adolescents? Why?
Which of your health aspects would you like to **improve**? How?

cards.q: How did W/ro Almaz's husband die?
cards.why: "Her husband died during the liberation war" (p. 2).

cards.title: A questionnaire
body: You read 10 statements and tick **Agree**, **Disagree** or **Not sure**.
Examples: "**Cooking is a girls' job.**" "**Education is not so important for girls.**"
Others: "**Nowadays boys and girls are sharing the household work.**"

cards.title: Sex and gender
body: The book asks you to think about the difference.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What is the difference between **biological (sex)** and **social (gender)** roles?
Who is more affected by health problems, **boys or girls**? Why?

cards.title: Make a list
body: Write and display **five things** healthy people **should do**.
Then **five things** they **shouldn't do**.
Choose the **ten best** health practices from all the lists.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: Do you do things you **know** are not good for your health? Why?
Which **unhealthy behaviours** are most common among young people? How can they change?

cards.title: Health promoting or demoting?
body: Draw a picture of each kind of school.

cards.title: Project
body: Discuss **how health promoting** your school is.
Come up with **five actions (strategies)** to make it more health promoting.

cards.title: A health club
body: Does your school have a **health club**?
If yes: how can it help? If no: how could one be started, and **who** should start it?
What should the **community** do to strengthen it?

glossary.meaning: a woman whose husband has died
the social roles of boys and girls
the biological difference of male and female
a list of questions or statements to answer
a school club that works for health
a young person growing into an adult

tips.text: Health has three aspects: **physical, mental, social**.
Read the cases: **who is more healthy?** Think of all three aspects.

units.title: Puberty
units.intro: **Puberty** is the time when a child's body starts to change into an adult's. This unit asks about **physical and behavioural changes**, **emotions and stress**, and **personal hygiene**.

pins.text: Haile, 15: he looks angry and pulls Dehab away
Zahra: "Everyone is laughing at me about my face."
Senait: "It is normal. It is a part of growing up."

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: You will look at **secondary sexual characteristics**: the body changes of puberty.
You will also look at **behaviour changes** and how to **cope with emotions and stress**.

cards.title: What this unit covers
body: Tap each part.

cards.title: Physical changes
body: **Girls' groups** list the physical changes in **boys**. **Boys' groups** list the changes in **girls**.
Then: which changes happen to **both** girls and boys?

cards.title: Behavioural changes
body: Groups list the **behaviour changes** of puberty.
What **causes** these changes?

cards.title: Think and talk
body: How can adolescents cope with **feeling shy**?
With a **strong attraction** to someone of the opposite sex?
With **wanting more independence**?

cards.title: A strong emotion
body: Remember a **strong emotion** you felt. Tell your group what it was, **what caused it**, and **what you did**.
Why is it important to **recognize** your emotions?

steps.text: At a **wedding**, Haile sees Dehab dancing with a boy about his age.
Haile looks **angry** and forces Dehab away through the crowd.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: If you were Haile, what would you do?
What advice could you give Dehab?
Is it easy to cope with **stress**? Why?

cards.title: Hygiene and body changes
body: The book asks about each of these.

cards.title: Menstruation: think and talk
body: Why do women menstruate? Is menstruation a **sickness**?
What are the best **hygiene practices** for a girl during menstruation?
How is menstruation related to **pregnancy**?

cards.title: Yonas
body: **Yonas** is **14**. He chats with **Almaz** at school and often dreams about her at night.
One morning he wakes up and finds his **underwear wet**.

cards.title: Wet dreams: think and talk
body: What happened to Yonas? Does this also happen to girls?
**Who** should you ask for more information?
What **hygiene practices** should people take?

steps.text: **Zahra** is sad. Everyone laughs at her **pimples**. Hair grows under her arms and sometimes she has a **bad smell**.
**Senait** says: "It is **normal**. It is a part of **growing up**."

cards.title: Is it fair?
body: Is it fair to **make fun** of someone with pimples or body smell?
How does poor **personal hygiene** affect relationships?

cards.q: What does Senait tell Zahra about pimples?

options.B: they are normal, part of growing up

cards.why: Senait: "But it is normal. It is a part of growing up." (p. 9)

a change in the way you act
a strong feeling, like anger or joy
a feeling of pressure or worry

a small spot on the skin

tips.text: Changes in puberty are **normal**: "a part of growing up".
Recognize your **emotions**; think before you act.
Keep good **personal hygiene**. Never make fun of others.

units.title: Nutrition
units.intro: This unit asks how **nutrients** relate to **health**, and how **food** is linked to **climate, age and sex**.

pins.text: Ato Musa and Fozia: lowlands; garden with green vegetables and fruits; drink a lot of water
Ato Ibrahim and Sofia: highlands; eat food that keeps them warm
climate: hot areas and cold areas
age: young people and old people
occupation: daily labourers and office workers

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: You will compare **nutrients** and **health**.
You will see how food is linked to **climate, age and sex**.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What are **nutrients**?
What is a **balanced diet**?

cards.title: Nutritional requirements
body: The book's table lists these five.

cards.title: The table
body: For **childhood**, **adolescents** and **old** people, write **high**, **moderate** or **low** for each nutrient.
Work it out in class with your teacher.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What would happen if you always eat the **same type of food**?
Which popular foods and drinks do **little** for young people's nutrition? Why are they popular?

cards.title: Factors
body: The book asks: what **factors** influence nutrition?

cards.title: Two families
body: Compare the two case studies.

cards.title: Case I: Ato Musa
body: Ato Musa and his wife **Fozia** have **five children**. They live in the **lowlands**.
Their garden gives **green vegetables and fruits**. They eat enough breakfast.
Lunch and dinner are **light and soft**. They drink **too much water**.

cards.title: Case II: Ato Ibrahim
body: Ato Ibrahim and his wife **Sofia** have **five children**. They live in the **highlands**.
They usually eat food that **keeps them warm**.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What food should Musa's family **reduce**? What should Ibrahim's family **include**? Why?
How does **climate** influence your food choices?

cards.title: Agree or disagree?
body: You read 9 statements and tick **Agree**, **Disagree** or **Not sure**.
Examples: "**Taking alcoholic drinks leads to health risks and other problems.**"
"**Milk products are recommended to adolescents each day.**"

cards.title: More statements
body: "**Obesity** in adolescents can bring psychological and social problems."
"Adolescents prefer foods which are chosen by their **peers**."
Discuss each one with your group and teacher.

lessons.title: Project: diet, climate, age and occupation

cards.title: Project: diet and...
body: Interview grandparents, elder neighbours or family friends.

cards.title: Interview questions
body: What food do people prefer in **hot** areas? In **cold** areas?
What food do **young** people prefer? **Old** people?
Who needs more energy: **daily labourers** or **office workers**? Why?

cards.title: Memory trick: C-A-O
body: Food depends on **C**limate, **A**ge and **O**ccupation.

cards.q: In the project, who does the book tell you to interview?

options.B: grandparents, elder neighbours or family friends

cards.why: p. 13: "by interviewing grand parents, elder neighbours or family friends".

one of the nutrients in the book's table

tips.text: Five nutrient groups in the table: **proteins, carbohydrates, fats and oils, vitamins, water**.
Food is linked to **climate, age and occupation**.
Always eating the **same food** is something to think about.

Ato Musa's family has a garden.
Ato Ibrahim's family eats light and soft food.

units.title: What are my values?
units.intro: What is a **value**? This unit asks you to rank values, look at messages from your **family**, **tradition**, **conflicting values**, and **media and peer pressure**.

pins.text: Ato Hagos and his wife, parents of six children
Habtom, the youngest, fetched water to wash hands
a guest arrives; the children are sent out
Awet: "It is time to try alcohol and cigarettes."
Sara: "I choose not to smoke and drink."
friends laugh and gossip about Sara and Musa's friendship
friends tell Musa he must make love to Sara to "show he is a man"
a friend uses a violent film to say alcohol makes you "brave"

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: You will describe what a **value** means.
You will explore values in your **society** and what **influences** them.

cards.title: Sixteen values to rank
body: Choose and rank the **five most important** values.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: Was it **easy** to agree when ranking values in your group? Why?

cards.title: Messages from your family about...
body: What does your family tell you about each one?

cards.title: Think and talk
body: Do **boys and girls** get different advice from their family?
Do **men** give different messages from **women**?
Do **younger** family members give different messages from **older** ones?

steps.text: Ato Hagos has **six children**. One Sunday his wife prepares **lunch**.
The youngest, **Habtom**, fetches **water** to wash hands.
A **guest** arrives. **All the children are sent out**. The guest admires the family's **hospitality**.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What do you think of sending the children out? What would **you** do?
How would you feel if your lunch was interrupted by a guest?
What values do the **family** and the **guest** show? Are they acceptable?

steps.text: **Awet**: "We are grown up. It is time to try **alcohol and cigarettes**." Even their friend **Thomas** smokes and drinks.
**Sara**: our **religion**, **tradition** and **family** forbid it. Alcohol and cigarettes **destroy our health and economy**.

cards.title: Sara's joke
body: Sara: "If God wanted me to smoke, he would have put a **chimney** on my head."
"If God wanted me to drink, he would have put a **barrel** in my stomach."

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What would you do if you were Awet or Sara? What advice for **Thomas**?
Is it good if your values are **dictated by others**?
How do you **maintain** your values?

steps.text: Friends **laugh and gossip** about Sara and Musa's friendship.
Musa's friends say he must **make love to Sara** to show he is a man.
Another friend points to a **film**: a drunk man attacked a school girl. He says alcohol makes you "brave".

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What **influences** affect Sara and Musa? Which is **strongest**?
What should you do when your values go **against** your friends' values?
How can you **resist** influences and keep good relationships?

cards.q: What did Musa do when his friends pressured him?

glossary.meaning: to put in order of importance
customs passed down in a society
to order what someone must do
talk about other people's private lives

tips.text: Know **your own values**, and rank what matters most.
Like Sara and Musa, you can **say no**.

"I choose not to smoke and drink"
a friend who smokes and drinks

units.title: Planning for the future
units.intro: This unit is about **goals**. It asks about **gender and goals**, and two **obstacles**: **substance abuse** and **stressors**.

pitch.title: Life is like a football game

pins.text: "fouls": what would they be in real life?
"penalties": what would they be in real life?
"Doctor, come quick, the patient is sick." "Ok! Nurse, calm down."
"Please finish typing this report before lunch." "Yes, boss."
"Why do I fail in Mathematics all the time?"
"The children should be back from school. Let me finish the cooking."
"The life of a soldier is tough but it is good to fight for your country."
Rahwa, grade 7, the most clever in her class, the eldest child
her father died in a car accident four months ago
she helps her mother by selling groundnuts
she has less time to study; her marks become low
she is planning to stop going to school

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: You will explain what a **goal**, a **stereotype** and **substance abuse** are.
You will identify **stressors** and ways to **cope** with them.

cards.title: Life is like a football game
body: The book compares life to football.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What is a **goal**? What is similar between **football** and **real life**?
What happens if a person tries and **fails** to reach a goal?
Can all goals be reached in the **same length of time**?

cards.title: Who said it?
body: Draw each situation and the people who spoke.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: When you drew the people, did you draw **men or women**? Why?
This activity helps you think about **stereotypes** and goals.

cards.title: Obstacles to goals
body: The book names two obstacles.

cards.title: Role play
body: Role play: try to **persuade a prize-winner student** to drink alcohol.
How does the student **say no**?

cards.title: Think and talk
body: How are young people **exposed** to substance abuse? What are its **effects**?
How can young people **keep their stand** against it?
How can substance abuse affect **your goals**?

cards.title: Not always easy
body: The book asks: is it always easy to reach your goals **as planned**? Why?

steps.text: **Rahwa** is in **grade 7**. She was the **most clever** in her class. She is the **eldest** child.
Her father died in a **car accident** four months ago.
She helps her mother by **selling groundnuts**.
She has less time to study. Her **marks become low**.
She is planning to **stop going to school**.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: What **stressors** did Rahwa face?
What **other stressors** can stop students reaching their goals?

cards.title: Memory trick: G-O-S
body: Set **G**oals, know the **O**bstacles, keep your **S**tand.

cards.q: Why does Rahwa have less time to study?

options.B: she helps her mother by selling groundnuts

cards.why: p. 20: "she has begun to help her mother by selling groundnuts."

a fixed idea about a group of people
the social roles of men and women

to try to make someone agree

tips.text: A goal is like a goal in football: there are **fouls** and **penalties** on the way.

games.title: Life is like a football game

items.text: Rahwa helps her mother by selling ___.
Rahwa is the youngest in her family.
Her father died in a car accident.
The book names substance abuse as an obstacle to goals.

questions.q: How did Rahwa's father die?
why: p. 20: "Her father died in a car accident four months ago."

similar.q: When?
similar.a: four months ago

questions.q: What is Rahwa planning to do?
why: p. 20: "she is planning to stop going to school."

similar.q: Why?
similar.a: her marks became low because she had no time to study

questions.q: Before her father died, Rahwa was...

options.A: the most clever one in her class

why: p. 20: "She was the most clever one in her class."

similar.q: Is she the eldest or youngest?
similar.a: the eldest

questions.q: Which two obstacles to goals does the book name?
why: p. 19–20: 5.3 "substance abuse" and 5.4 "stressors".

similar.q: What role play does 5.3 suggest?
similar.a: persuading a prize winner student to drink alcohol

questions.q: In football there are "fouls" and "penalties". The book asks what these would be in...
why: p. 18: "what would this be in real life?"

similar.q: What else does the book ask about football?
similar.a: the similarities between a football game and real life

questions.q: One situation in 5.2 is "Why do I fail in Mathematics all the time?"
why: p. 19, situation c.

similar.q: Who says "Yes, boss"?
similar.a: the person typing the report

questions.q: In the role play, you try to persuade a ___ student to drink alcohol.
why: p. 19: "Try to persuade a prize winner student to drink alcohol."

similar.q: How can substance abuse affect your goals?
similar.a: the book asks you to discuss

questions.q: Which words does this unit want you to explain?
why: p. 18, learning outcome: "Explain what a goal, stereotype and substance abuse are".

similar.q: What else will you identify?
similar.a: stressors and ways of coping with them

questions.q: Mention the stressors Rahwa faced.
questions.answer: Her father's death, having to sell groundnuts to help her mother, less time to study, and low marks.
why: p. 20: the story.
questions.tip: List what changed in her life.

similar.q: Name another stressor for students.
similar.a: your own answer

questions.q: What will happen if a person tries and fails to achieve a goal?
questions.answer: Your own answer; discuss with your group (think of a football team that loses and tries again).
why: p. 18, Question 4. The book gives no model answer.

similar.q: Can all goals be achieved in the same time?
similar.a: the book asks you to discuss why
